designIntent: Cocoa & Chrome is a polished modern house built around smoky gray-brown oak, reflective silver metals, white upholstery and light warm putty/pearl walls. Blue belongs in artwork and removable textiles; butter-yellow is a smaller removable accent. Plants supply green. Do not introduce Mineral & Walnut’s walnut furniture, golden metal, brown plaster recipe or its approved A/C1/E stone selections.
sourcePriority: Latest user functional/blueprint corrections and actual owned inventory 29 types/39 units.
Original white-brick model-home photographs and current verified shell cameras establish openings and geometry.
Cocoa & Chrome owner-furniture brief and cabinet-variety revision for palette and new joinery design.
Older Cocoa & Chrome images are style references only where their shell or product inventory is stale.

CC-W1.appearance: Smooth light warm putty/pearl greige, with enough tonal depth to distinguish the white upholstery. No cloudy cream-beige plaster effect.
CC-W1.approach: Premium washable matte acrylic paint. Benjamin Moore Aura Matte is the sample system; Pale Oak OC-20 and Balboa Mist OC-27 are competing large-board color candidates, not final selected colors. Choose one connected-floor neutral after looking beside the actual Brown Oak, polished stainless, white fabric and daylight.
CC-W1.substrate: Inspect and repair existing drywall/plaster, resolve moisture causes, fill and sand defects, use substrate-compatible primer and follow the current paint data sheet for preparation, coats and curing. Skim only the affected visible areas where raking light reveals defects. A smooth finish does not require a decorative mineral-plaster coating.
CC-W1.sampleApproval: Approve large movable boards in morning, afternoon and artificial light. Record exact product, color code, sheen and batch before ordering.

CC-W2.surface: Trim, light interior doors and ceilings
CC-W2.appearance: Soft warm white; ceilings flat, doors and trim a clean low satin. Clear gallery door glass stays clear.
CC-W2.approach: Manufacturer-compatible trim enamel on prepared existing wood/MDF and flat ceiling paint. White Dove OC-17 is a sample candidate only. Preserve existing crown and ceiling profiles.
CC-W2.substrate: Degloss and clean old coatings as required; inspect adhesion, fill joints correctly and prime repaired or bare substrate. Do not paint door glass, hinges, smoke devices or vents shut.

CC-O1.surface: Dry interior floors and stair treads
CC-O1.appearance: Light-to-medium neutral natural white-oak appearance, matte and visibly lighter than the smoky furniture; restrained grain and knots. Neither gray vinyl nor orange/honey oak.
CC-O1.approach: Assess the existing floor construction, wear layer, moisture and condition before deciding to refinish or replace. For replacement use a sample-approved engineered oak system appropriate to the subfloor; dimensions, grade, wear layer and installation method remain to be selected. Coordinate a consistent finished-floor height and actual transitions.
CC-O1.substrate: Flooring contractor checks flatness, moisture, acclimation and manufacturer installation instructions. Complete dirty rough work before finish flooring. Protect finished floors without trapping moisture. Match stair stain by a full tread sample.
CC-O1.stairRule: No stair runners, stair rods or adhesive tread carpets. Preserve the actual quarter-turn/half-landing/straight-flight shape and compliant handrail/guard. Installer to address any required traction detail without inventing a runner.

CC-J1.appearance: Smoky BROWN OAK with gray/charcoal undertones and recognizable open oak grain. Satin-matte protective finish. New floor-standing storage has a continuous recessed/flush plinth; no spindly feet or floating storage.
CC-J1.approach: Use sound existing or standard cabinet boxes where practical, with sample-approved brown-oak veneer/solid edging and varied fronts: calm slab doors, limited thin frames, a few reeded-glass uppers or display doors. Polished stainless pulls, edge grips or fine reveals are selective accents. Do not repeat full-width metal drawer bands throughout the house.
CC-J1.substrate: Cabinetmaker to specify stable carcasses, veneer lay-up, concealed attachment, service access, ventilation, edge sealing and finished plinths. Keep doors/drawers serviceable after flooring. Provide shop drawings before fabrication.
CC-J1.ownedException: The actual owned Bezier and Machinto pieces keep their authentic fronts, supports, metal bands and bases. Maslow’s Espresso Walnut/Polished Aluminum and Cabrera’s Charcoal Waxed Concrete are actual owned exceptions. Never remodel owned furniture to look like the new joinery rule.

CC-S1.surface: Kitchen and wet-room counters; selected focal porcelain
CC-S1.appearance: Quiet pearl-white to light warm gray Carrara-like porcelain or a low-contrast white/gray engineered counter surface. Fine gray veining, low contrast, no gold/rust veining, heavy onyx clouding or tan limestone scheme.
CC-S1.approach: Kitchen counter finish is a practical sample-approved quartz or porcelain surface after comparing fabrication cost and existing-box condition. Wet walls use an actual rated porcelain tile/slab product; Daltile’s marble-look collections are sourcing leads rather than a final named SKU. Consider satin/honed-looking wall surfaces and a suitable matte wet-floor version; never assume a polished wall slab is an appropriate slip-resistant floor.
CC-S1.substrate: Tile/slab installer and fabricator coordinate approved backer, waterproofing where wet, substrate flatness, joint layout, reinforcement, edge details, cutouts and movement joints under the chosen system instructions. Approve a full actual tile/slab and seam drawing.
CC-S1.hierarchy: Kitchen uses the quietest fine gray vein. Owners bath may have slightly broader pearl-gray movement. Shared and smaller baths use calmer economical field tiles. Fireplace remains a restrained pearl-gray surround, not an extravagant bookmatched statement. No automatic transfer of Option 1 studies A, C 1 or E.

CC-M1.appearance: Actual owned polished stainless and polished nickel govern the nearby finish samples. New fittings may use polished stainless, polished nickel or chrome when sample coordinated.
CC-M1.approach: Choose one compatible polished-silver finish family per room. Match appearance by real samples; stainless, nickel and chrome are not chemically identical finishes. Keep black limited to AV, piano, selected chair supports and thin art frames. No new brass/gold fixtures.
CC-M1.care: Use each manufacturer’s cleaning directions. Do not spray abrasive or acidic cleaners across polished metal or stone.

CC-T1.appearance: Warm-white/ecru linen-look ripple-fold sheers; hidden off-white opaque/privacy layers and true blackout where required. Ivory/stone rugs with subtle taupe/gray texture. White upholstery, a few ink/slate/soft-blue textiles and a smaller butter-yellow highlight.
CC-T1.approach: Curtain workroom measures actual glazing, curve/arch heads, side returns, stackback, track support and finished floor. Sheers are not a night-privacy specification. Keep a wood border around each bedroom rug; exact rug sizes and actual owned fabrics govern.
CC-T1.sampleApproval: Approve curtain fabric against the owned White Italian Textured Weave and White Perennials. Check opacity with a lamp at night; view full panel and blackout side-gap sample.

CC-G1.appearance: Quiet charcoal/black rubber, with clean perimeter and no area rug.
CC-G1.approach: Select an indoor rubber product suitable for the existing subfloor, expected use and odor requirements. Confirm adhesive, expansion and moisture preparation with its manufacturer. No equipment is included in this design.

CC-X1.appearance: Preserve the actual white-brick house, roof forms, deck, railings and established pergola/shade sails. The selected new Malibu furnishings use Black powder-coated outdoor aluminum and separately purchased White outdoor cushions, with restrained removable blue/butter-yellow accents and green planters. Do not substitute the prior teak scheme or indoor stainless furniture.
CC-X1.approach: No indoor oak veneer, normal interior paint, indoor curtains or indoor furniture outdoors. Confirm wind, drainage, loads, fastening, corrosion and maintenance with the appropriate trades. Existing deck/roof repairs are surveyed separately; no new roof geometry is proposed.

Shell: Keep the one real centered paired 2 × 2 window; sofa-side wall is solid because the facade feature there is false. Preserve clear WEST gallery doors near the TV-wall corner. Do not enlarge the nominal 133-inch seating wall, add a window behind the sofa, relocate the doors or cut into the shared office wall. Display sits to the right of doors when seen from inside the media room. Final depth/width follow AV equipment and site clearance; do not fabricate 108–120 inches automatically. Mount the 83-inch TV on a restrained pearl-gray paint or quiet thin porcelain panel with a soft serviceable warm LED halo behind its edge. No busy wood-slat background, sharp gold veins or enlarged wall box. Keep the soundbar externally visible and its driver paths free. Add shallow lit collectible niches near the west doors using limited smoky-oak shelf frames and discreet silver trim. Do not reduce the door opening or create a giant second cabinetry wall. Generous new cinema sofa must fit the 133-inch seating envelope. A 119-inch straight sofa leaves about 7 inches per end before actual casing/clearance; no 18-inch end tables beyond it.
